_comment_tint: WO-F09-05 round 2: pockets[].lamp_tint recolours that pocket's mouth lamps, junction lamps and reward glow, so each gate differs slightly from the others. Warm amber, moss green-gold, pale storm cyan, warm white and gold: never red (Team Tether) or magenta (the strike telegraph).
_comment: WORLD §5.1 dead-end pockets (coordinator ruling: a walled dead-end clearing of installed static walls or deadwood with an existing reward moved inside counts; a pickup grid point does not). Each pocket is a 16 x 16 m clearing walled on every side by a dead-trunk palisade with one 5 m mouth facing its nearest road. mouth_yaw_deg is the horizontal direction from the centre out through the mouth (0 = +Z, 90 = +X). The reward is an existing optional_reward_pocket pickup from the same region, moved inside.

approach_clear._comment: The mouth reads down its spur: the forest bake keeps every tree and colliding rock out of a cone that starts mouth_half_width_m either side of the mouth and widens by half_angle_deg out to length_m, and keeps ground cover out of its first ground_cover_length_m.

spur_junction_clear._comment: WO-F09-05 round 2 (blind judge: from the road the spur mouth reads as a streetlight in grass). The forest bake keeps ground cover (ferns, bushes, mushrooms) off each spur's first length_m, within half_width_m of its centre line, and out of a ground_cover_radius_m disc round the junction; trees and colliding rocks keep out of a tree_radius_m disc round the junction, so the junction lamps stand against open ground.

mouth_lure._comment: Two wayfinding lamps flank each mouth: the installed wall lantern with an amber flame and a short warm light, the vocabulary of the Stormheart ascent lamps (stormheart_tree.gd). Each hangs from a wooden post (Stormheart bark finish, with its own static collider) standing against the wall's outer face just beyond the mouth edge, and faces out along the approach. lantern_mount_height_m is the bracket's base above the ground.

spur_marker._comment: One more lamp post marks where each pocket's spur route (stormwood_world.json kind spur) leaves its road: along_m up the spur from the junction, clear of the road's 7.5 m corridor, and side_m to the spur's right so it stands on the verge of the painted spur lane (stormwood_road_surface.json), inside the spur's tree-cleared corridor. Its lantern faces back toward the road. WO-F09-04: `lamp` overrides mouth_lure for this post only so the junction lamp reads from the road at 30 m by day: the lantern head sits at about 2.5x the 1.80 m trainer, the post is pale weathered wood that separates from dark trunks, the flame is unshaded (it keeps its colour in sun and shade) and an additive glow billboard of halo_radius_m stands in for the bloom the Compatibility renderer lacks. Same installed lantern, bark finish and amber flame as the mouth lamps and the Stormheart ascent lamps.
spur_marker._comment_pair: WO-F09-05 round 2 (blind judge: a single lamp beside the road read as a streetlight in grass): two junction posts now frame the spur like a gateway, one either side of its painted lane, side_clear_m outside the lane edge (spur width plus junction flare there), at the first distance from along_m to along_max_m up the spur where both clear every through road's corridor (terrain route_half_width + road_clear_m), capped own_corridor_margin_m inside the spur's own corridor. stormwood_pockets.gd spur_posts().

reward_beacon._comment: WO-F09-05 round 2 (blind judge: nothing visible from the gate is worth the detour). Each pocket's reward pickup is drawn model_scale_mul larger and carries its pocket's lamp tint as a warm light pool (OmniLight light_height_m above it, no shadow) and an additive glow billboard, both children of the pickup so they leave with it when it is claimed. stormwood_pickup_runtime.gd; the shared ItemCachePickup is not edited.

draw_distance._comment: Palisade trunks and lamp art stop drawing past models_m, fading over models_fade_m; each lamp's OmniLight fades out over lights_fade_m ending at lights_m (a light has no visibility range).
